bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion and 18 consecutive quarters of growth indicate strong patient uptake and effective commercialization. Continued U.S. adoption, international sales and repeat neurologist prescribing support a durable growth base for the next several quarters.

Extremely low leverage and substantial liquidity give argenx flexibility to fund late-stage trials, manufacturing and global commercialization without near-term financing dependence. This financial capacity strengthens resilience while the company broadens its immunology portfolio.

Positive pivotal myositis data provide a credible route to another labeled indication for VYVGART and expand the addressable market beyond current neuromuscular uses. Durable efficacy through one year, including during steroid tapering, supports potential clinical differentiation.

bear.b: Although cash generation improved sharply in 2025, the multi-year record remains inconsistent and operating cash flow has not fully matched accounting earnings. Sustained profitability and better conversion are important to reduce reliance on the current cash reserve.

argenx is investing heavily in clinical development and commercialization, which can compress margins and raise execution requirements. The spending is strategically directed, but revenue growth must continue at scale to offset costs and preserve the recent profitability inflection.

Persistent payer restrictions and physician treatment habits may limit earlier-line CIDP penetration, extending the time needed to realize the indication’s full potential. These access barriers can constrain growth even when clinical evidence supports broader use.
